say: The mine door. Plate steel, set into a timber frame, set into the rock.
A weld bead runs all the way round the frame. Bright, unweathered. On this side.
Stacked against the rock beside it: rescue stretchers, still in their wrap. Never opened.
Nobody seals a collapse from the outside before the rescue crews have been in.
The weld is cold. You put your ear to the steel anyway. Rain, and your own pulse.
